title: Derived pullback and open extension transport explicit etale-origin witnesses
statement:
Use the finite coefficient datum $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $u:U\to X$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$, $i:U\hookrightarrow V$ open immersions into separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use constant-$A$ module sheaves and the bounded-below derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ have the explicit etale-origin witness $(L,\alpha)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], with $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $\alpha:\nu_X^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}K$.

The canonical sheaf comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] induces a natural derived isomorphism
$$\kappa_u:\nu_U^*u_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}Lu^*\nu_X^*.$$
For every open immersion $e:S\hookrightarrow T$ among $i,j$, the sheaf comparison of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] induces a natural derived isomorphism
$$\delta_e:\nu_T^*e^{\mathrm{et}}_!\xrightarrow{\sim}e^{\mathrm{proet}}_!\nu_S^*$$
on $D^+(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$; both open extensions are applied degreewise [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. These maps are the maps induced by their termwise sheaf comparisons on localization at quasi-isomorphisms, independently of the representing complexes. Put $L_u=u_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}L$ and $M=Lu^*K$. Then the following displayed pairs are etale-origin witnesses on the indicated schemes:
$$
\begin{aligned}
M &: (L_u,\alpha_u),\qquad \alpha_u=(Lu^*\alpha)\circ\kappa_{u,L},\\
j_!K &: (j^{\mathrm{et}}_!L,\ j_!\alpha\circ\delta_{j,L}),\\
i_!M &: (i^{\mathrm{et}}_!L_u,\ i_!\alpha_u\circ\delta_{i,L_u}).
\end{aligned}
$$
All these objects and witnesses are bounded below.
